violet: hey all, brand new here. first-week build from source went fine but running kv_cache unit test crashes immediately. not sure if it's my local container or something I messed up. any pointers? :wave:

violet: output:

violet: ```
$ ./bazel-bin/runtime/tests/kv_cache_test --gtest_filter=KVCache.*
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
#0  0x7f71e2b12e in ?? () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
#1  0x560d3f2a9f in runtime::gpu::DeviceTracker::init
#2  0x560d3f2b30 in runtime::kv::Store::append
```

violet: ldd shows libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found inside the container, even though `nvidia-smi` on the host returns Driver 535.86 / CUDA 12.2.

mika: welcome! common new-hire trap: dev containers often don't include/mount the host driver libs. two quick checks: `ldd` as you did, and `LD_DEBUG=libs` to see dlopen attempts.

tiago: if you can, try creating the expected symlink inside the container pointing to the vendor lib (e.g. libnvidia-ml.so.535.86 -> libnvidia-ml.so.1) or run the container with `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` mounted from the host. that usually fixes missing-dlopen issues.

violet: made the symlink and ldd resolves now, but it still crashes with NVML call in the bt (nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex...).

mika: could be ABI/driver mismatch or our code hitting NVML too early (static ctor or global singleton). for quick repro do: 1) set `NVML_INJECTION_DISABLED=1` to skip NVML probes for local runs; 2) run under gdb with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to get reliable backtrace; 3) try LD_PRELOAD pointing at the host lib if versions differ.

tiago: also grep tests for any global `DeviceTracker` or calls during static init. some test harnesses register globals that call the GPU init path before env vars are read. if that's the case, a tiny test harness change to delay probe helps onboarding.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-561: "onboard: kv_cache crash in dev container - NVML/driver mismatch" assigned to infra oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-561 :ticket:

devex: added onboarding note: if you see NVML dlopen/segfaults in first-week builds, try the `redwood/dev-container:gpu-dev` image or mount host drivers; `NVML_INJECTION_DISABLED` can be used temporarily. link: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/runtime-dev#gpu-drivers

violet: thanks, i'll try gdb + the gpu-dev image and link the ticket if infra needs to change mounts. really appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
